page: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v6 is a Dplsv6-series virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores using the ARM64 architecture, specifically powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory profile of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory subsystem performance is also highly rated, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaching top-tier levels. However, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average category.

The primary tradeoff of the D64pls_v6 is its low memory-to-core ratio and the absence of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX, AVX-512, or AMX. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides high resource density and excellent multi-threaded compute performance per resource unit, making it highly efficient for parallelized workloads that do not require large memory footprints.

This server is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data processing. It is also capable of handling moderate large language model inference tasks and redis operations, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or single-threaded applications.
